newsitem.title: USA: Warmer weather seen easing travel on Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Warmer weather seen easing travel on Illinois.

text.p: Rising temperatures in the U.S. Midwest have generated expectations for smoother travel on the Illinois River by early next week, river dealers and officials said.
"Let's hope that the warmer weather stays through the weekend," said one dealer on the northern Illinois. "Then, by the first of next week, we should have good (barge) movement."
In response, values for corn and soybeans along the river were slightly lower on Friday, cash sources said.
Soybean CIF basis bids for February fell one cent to 37 cents per bushel over March Chicago Board of Trade futures.
Additionally, some cash grain merchandisers lowered basis bids for corn by several cents per bushel on Friday because of the expected increase in movement.
"Barge values collapsed on Thursday and some of the ice is breaking up on the Illinois (River) so there is more movement," said one Cincinnati-based dealer.

U.S. forecasters show temperatures climbing into the 50s (Fahrenheit) in southern Illinois on Saturday and Sunday, and temperatures in the northern half of the state should be in the 40s, according to National Weather Service forecasts.

On the Illinois, north of Peoria as far north as Ottawa, most channels were clear, so traffic should be able to get through, said Rick Granados, chief of the lock and dam section for the Army Corps of Engineers in Peoria, Ill.
"It (traffic) seems to be doing pretty well this morning (Friday)," Granados said. "There's ice, but traffic is shooting along at a pretty good clip."
However, some river dealers warned that barge travel on the Illinois was still hindered because of the ice and transit times were very slow.

Traffic was said to be moving with few problems on the Mississippi River south of St. Louis. All traffic north of St. Louis will be shut off until lock 22 near Hannibal, Mo. is reopened on Saturday, river officials said.
